terms.gloss: the iris, a plant prized for its scented root
evidence: Plin. NH 21.41: flōret versicolōrī speciē, sīcut arcus caelestis, unde et nōmen
terms.comment: The same word as the goddess Iris and the rainbow, from which Pliny says the flower has its name. Pliny values it for its root alone, used in perfumes and medicine, the best from Illyricum (NH 21.40); Columella puts the Illyrian iris among the scents for wine. Lewis & Short’s identification is doubtful (“perh. the sword-lily”); botanists give the name to the genus Iris. Lewis & Short gives the genitive īris or īridis; Pliny writes īridis.

phrases.latin: caulem habet cubitālem, ērēctum; flōret versicolōrī speciē, sīcut arcus caelestis, unde et nōmen.
phrases.english: It has an upright stem a cubit high, and flowers in many colours, like the rainbow, from which it has its name.

sources: Lewis & Short: iris
